source.title: Scaling Synthetic-Image Pre-Training for Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Vision Models
source.authors: Qian-Piao Ma; Xiao-Zhu Song; Jun-Long Zhou; Yue Zeng; Jian-Chun Liu; Hua-Qing Tu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figures and table layouts are garbled in the extracted text, but the relevant scaling-law results are also described in text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper invokes prior scaling-law work and develops its own scaling rule to choose synthetic-image volume for federated fine-tuning. It does not measure the language-model loss or scaling behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a fitted relationship between synthetic-image scaling factor, target accuracy, and total completion time, plus generation-time results. These measure a different outcome and scaling setup from the claim's language-model held-out cross-entropy laws, so they are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. Comparisons of FeDiSyn with other methods and its ablations are not rows because they report performance of the proposed method and its components, not the claimed language-model behavior.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as background and names its own fitted equation a 'scaling law'. That equation, Eq. 13, models total completion time (generation plus pre-training plus federated fine-tuning) as a function of synthetic-image scaling factor λ and target accuracy, for ViT classifiers. It measures no held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute. It does not extrapolate a loss law, allocate compute, vary model shape, test the loss power-law form in vision, or relate downstream performance to scale or loss. It also does not apply the claimed laws as a tool, so this is T6 rather than T4. Its findings are a different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that their fitted rule picks a synthetic-image volume balancing generation and pre-training cost against federated fine-tuning time, and λ* gives the shortest completion time of the values tested. They also conclude the full FeDiSyn framework cuts completion time by over 52.5% and traffic by over 97.2% against baselines, at comparable accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits a custom equation for total completion time as a function of synthetic-image scaling factor and target accuracy in federated image-model training; it does not use the language-model held-out-loss scaling-law measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted coefficients are reported separately for CIFAR-10, Caltech-101, and Food-101. The total completion time changes across the tested synthetic-image scaling factors.

fits_no_version.finding: Eq. 13, H = h0·λ + κ1·λ^(−κ2)·e^(κ3·Acc) + κ4, is fitted by nonlinear least squares on small λ. It gives dataset-specific coefficients (CIFAR-10, Caltech-101, Food-101), and the authors say it describes time, accuracy and data volume well.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In federated fine-tuning of ViTs, total completion time is U-shaped in synthetic-image volume, and a fitted power-exponential form locates its minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: On Food-101, generation time grows linearly with λ (5,050s to 20,200s). Time to 80% accuracy is shortest at λ* (17,584s), compared with 36,351s at 0.5λ* and 27,944s at 2λ*.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More synthetic pre-training data speeds federated fine-tuning with diminishing returns, while its generation cost grows linearly.

record.problems: The scaling-law evidence is for synthetic-image volume, classification accuracy, and completion time rather than language-model held-out loss. The fitted equation is calibrated from small-scale pilot runs; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the coefficients or completion-time results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed claim versions were reported. Performance and ablation comparisons in Sections 6.2 and Figs. 8–11, 14–15 concern the proposed federated-learning framework and are outside the claim's language-model loss measures.

untested.parts: No sweep of held-out pretraining loss over parameters, data or compute.
Eq. 13 is fitted on small λ and used to pick λ*, but this predicts completion time in one setting, not the loss of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute split between parameters and tokens.
No depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count. LoRA depth is varied for fine-tuning efficiency, not pretraining loss.
Vision models and fine-tuning are used, but no power-law fit of loss against model or data scale is made. Eq. 13 mixes a power of λ with an exponential in accuracy and targets time.
Model scale is not varied systematically. ViT-B and ViT-L are paired with different datasets, so accuracy against scale or pretraining loss is not testable.
Dataset-specific coefficients exist only for the paper's own time equation, not for the claimed loss exponents or the compute-optimal split.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (uses_without_test, T4) is changed to cites_only, T6. The paper neither applies nor tests the language-model laws; the shared term 'scaling law' is the only link. The ablation's remark that synthetic pre-training matters more for larger models confounds model size with dataset (ViT-B on CIFAR and Caltech, ViT-L on Food-101), so it cannot bear on any version. No coefficient uncertainties are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute sweep, or bottleneck-independent power-law fit is measured.
No predictions from small language-model runs are compared with substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between language-model parameters and training tokens is measured.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at a fixed parameter count is reported.

The study concerns image models and federated fine-tuning, but measures accuracy and completion time against synthetic-image volume rather than testing whether the claimed held-out-loss power-law form transfers to these settings.
The study reports classification accuracy against elapsed time, but does not test downstream-task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.

Dataset-specific coefficients are reported for the paper's different empirical equation, but the study does not test setup- or fitting-dependence of the claimed language-model exponents or compute-optimal parameter/token split.

rows.operation_detail: Fit the paper's total-completion-time equation against synthetic-image scaling factor and target accuracy.
